name: Rune-Inscribed Parchment
summary: In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives aspiring orc shamans a summons from Shikrik. It calls them to guide their people and commune with elemental spirits.

sections.title: A Summons to the Spirits
sections.body:
New orc shamans train under veteran overseers in the Valley of Trials. During an initiate’s first trials, Gornek gives them a rune-covered message from Shikrik, the local shamanic instructor. It calls them to deepen their bond with the elements.

Among the orcs, shamans mediate between the living and their ancestors. The message marks a turn from brute strength toward disciplined reverence for ancestral ways.

faq.answer: In the Valley of Trials, Gornek gives novice orc shamans a handwritten message. It directs them to report to Shikrik for formal instruction.
Shikrik, the shaman trainer in the Valley of Trials, wrote the parchment. It instructs young initiates in the ways of the elements and ancestral spirits.

faq.q: Why are shamans considered chosen among the orcs?
faq.answer: Orc shamans guide their people as spiritual leaders. They listen to elemental spirits and act as conduits for their ancestors. Shikrik teaches apprentices to mend allies and wield the elements’ fury against their foes.

angles.text: As a shaman, you take your first step on the path of the elements. Under Shikrik’s guidance, you learn ancestor worship and mastery of the elements.
As an orc, you carry ancestral wisdom in Durotar. The rediscovery of shamanic tradition is central to the new Horde.
